data.title: FOMC Will Need to Raise Interest Rate 'Soon' to Tame Inflation, St. Louis Fed's Musalem Says
data.description:
03:33 PM EDT, 10/30/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The Federal Reserve will likely need to tighten monetary policy "soon" to bring inflation down to its 2% target in a timely manner, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said Friday.

Earlier this week, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate steady in a divided decision. The dissenters, Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, preferred a second consecutive 25-basis-point hike at the meeting, the FOMC said Wednesday.

Current monetary policy continues to be accommodative, Musalem said Friday in remarks prepared for delivery at an event in New York.

"I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said.

He will become an FOMC voting member in 2028.

Markets are pricing in a 70% probability that the Fed will raise interest rate by 25 basis points in December, with the remaining odds in favor of a pause, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"The short-run economic costs of reducing inflation are less when the central bank acts before inflation has become entrenched and is expected to persist," Musalem said. "Acting sooner and incrementally now is likely to be less disruptive or costly than delaying and being forced to take large, abrupt actions later."

Inflation is elevated and broad based, with the headline and core prices continuing to run at 3% or above, Musalem said. Core inflation excludes the volatile food and energy components.

"I perceive meaningful risk that above-target inflation will persist longer than consistent with price stability," he said.

Musalem outlined two inflation scenarios for the next 18 months, with the more likely one envisaging high prices if the Fed doesn't tighten policy further, Musalem said.

However, if inflation pressures ease due to factors including lower energy prices, further policy firming won't be needed, he said, adding that such a scenario is "less likely but plausible."

The US economy remains resilient, while the labor market is "balanced around full employment," Musalem said.

"The (artificial intelligence-driven) boom in capital expenditures and wealth effects-driven consumption spending might slow from their current pace, but are likely to remain a tailwind for some time," he said. "Corporate earnings have been strong -- unusually so for this stage in the business cycle."

On Thursday, official data showed the US economy grew at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter, marking the strongest growth since the same quarter of 2025, aided by robust consumer spending.

data.title: White House hearing on Fed's Cook delayed to December, Hassett says
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The White House has delayed until December a planned hearing into allegations of mortgage fraud by Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, President Donald Trump's top economic advisor said, though lawyers for Cook on Friday declined to confirm that any date had been agreed. 

"The president has asked a small set of his people to run a completely fair process that puts all the information on the table, and then the president will decide next steps," Kevin Hassett told Bloomberg TV on Thursday. "We in the White House, the White House counsel, has worked very closely with Governor Cook's people. I think that they've agreed to a date in December to meet together and talk these things through." 

Cook's lawyer, who along with Cook herself has denied any wrongdoing and called Trump's accusations a pretense to remove her because he wants the Fed to cut rates, had previously said Cook would not be available for any hearing until after the Fed's December 8-9 policy-setting meeting. A spokeswoman for her lawyer did not confirm any new date in December. 

Trump has been trying to fire Cook for more than a year. 

The Supreme Court in June ruled that he cannot do so "at will" but that he may be able to if he gives her a chance to defend herself against any evidence he believes shows "cause" for removal. Trump announced a fresh investigation last month and initially set November 5 as a hearing date. 

Cook this week dissented on the Fed's decision to leave rates steady instead of delivering another rate hike to curb inflation, as she would have preferred. The Fed is widely expected to raise rates again in December. Trump has long railed against the Fed for not cutting rates, and accused a "political" Fed Board, which includes Cook, for keeping Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh from doing so. 

Hassett, who is on the three-person committee Trump appointed to investigate Cook and recommend if she should be fired, had called Cook "partisan" last August for not vacating her post after Trump's allegations.

On Thursday he told Bloomberg TV Thursday he feels "Chairman Warsh has done a good job of allowing, you know, normal dissent and then driving a consensus." 

The White House committee looking into Cook is comprised of "people of honor who are charged with looking at the evidence and correctly characterizing it in a way that people will be able to observe and criticize if they like," he said. 

(Reporting by Ann Saphir; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The US State Department said on Friday it had approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion.

Ukraine will pay for the missiles with contributions from Canada, Germany and Norway routed through the US JUMPSTART program, along with national funds financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan, the State Department said in a statement. 

Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the sale.

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said earlier this week that Ukraine had been waiting for almost a month for the US to sign off on critical ​missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

The Ukrainian leader has ​repeatedly called on the US, which supplies missiles purchased by ​NATO allies under a program known as PURL, to speed up deliveries ahead of winter.

(Reporting by Ryan Patrick Jones and Christian Martinez, editing by Michelle Nichols)

data.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record heist blamed on North Korea
data.description:
BOSTON/SINGAPORE/PARIS, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.

Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets. 

The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, but Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X that $3 billion represented only about 2% of the company's total user assets and public reserves. 

Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

Binance other co-CEO, Richard Teng, said in a post on X that the breach as a "complex attack" that was not carried out by one person and included a compromised laptop as well as malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity as it went along, "making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate."

The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, internet-connected so-called "hot" wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said.

"Rest assured that we are working non-stop to resolve this, to make the users whole, and live up to your trust," Teng wrote.

'LARGEST KNOWN THEFT'

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. 

"This incident is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind," British blockchain analysts Elliptic said.

The bulk of the Binance heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.

North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to US and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts.

North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.    

"When North Korea steals at this scale, the money supports weapons proliferation, which makes this a national security issue, not just a crypto theft," Ari Redbord, global head of policy and government affairs at TRM, said.

Binance is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Secret Service (USSS), a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.

The FBI said it was "aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps." 

The USSS said in a statement that its investigators "are working around the clock with our private-sector partners, including Circle, to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance on Thursday."

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

Abu Dhabi's Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance's main operating licence, said it was "engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident". Abu Dhabi-backed investment group MGX declined to comment. It became a minority investor in Binance last year. 

Crypto prices fell broadly but losses were contained.

Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised. Bitcoin last stood at $77,355 and ether at $2,229. Binance's BNB token was down 6.74% over the past 24 hours at $698.

SECURITY IMPLICATIONS

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group.

Investor Michael Saylor, among Bitcoin's most prominent supporters, said in a post on X that he expected Binance to "deliver" on ensuring no customers suffered losses. "Our industry will learn from this incident, strengthen security, and emerge stronger and more resilient," he wrote on Friday. 

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. 

(Reporting by Tom Westbrook, Ankur Banerjee and Rae Wee in Singapore, Summer Zhen in Hong Kong, Rocky Swift in Tokyo, Vallari Srivastava and Anusha Shah in Bengaluru and Mrinmay Dey in Mexico City, Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris, Tom Wilson in London, AJ Vicens in Detroit and Lawrence Delevingne in Boston; Writing by Lawrence Delevingne, Scott Murdoch and Tom Westbrook. Editing by Stephen Coates, Mark Potter, Elisa Martinuzzi, Tommy Reggiori Wilkes and David Gaffen)

data.title: CANADA FX DEBT-Canadian dollar extends monthly gain as higher oil prices raise inflation risk
data.description:
TORONTO, Oct 30 (Reuters) - The Canadian dollar strengthened to a six-week high against its US counterpart on Friday as a jump in oil prices supported bets the Bank of Canada would tighten further, overshadowing disappointing GDP data.

The loonie was trading 0.2% higher at 1.3955 per US dollar, or 71.66 US cents, after touching its strongest intraday level since September 16 at 1.3943. For the month, the currency was on track to gain 2%, which would be its biggest monthly advance since April.

* Canada's economy stalled in August for the second straight month, while advance estimates showed GDP declining 0.1% in September and annualized third-quarter growth of 1.3%. The BoC has projected the economy growing by 2% in the third quarter.

* "Markets ignored Canadian GDP and with good reason," Derek Holt, head of capital markets economics at Scotiabank, said in a note.

* "While the figures disappointed somewhat, the BoC is forward-looking and focused upon rising inflation risk that has many complex drivers - like oil that is fired up this morning," Holt said.

* On Wednesday, the Bank of Canada hiked its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% and said further increases might be needed to prevent soaring energy costs from driving broader inflation.

* Investors see a roughly 50% chance the central bank tightens at its next policy decision in December and have fully discounted a move by January.

* US crude oil futures were trading 2.7% higher at $104.80 a barrel as traders braced for a potential escalation in the US-Iran conflict after the US midterm elections. Oil is one of Canada's major exports.

* Canadian bond yields eased across a steeper curve as a sharp selloff in technology-related stocks pushed investors into safe-haven assets such as US Treasuries.

* The 10-year was down 2.1 basis points at 3.780%, after earlier touching its lowest level since September 4 at 3.768%.

(Reporting by Fergal Smith; Editing by Nia Williams)

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall Street slides as AI cash burn worries spark tech selloff
data.description:
(Updates to midafternoon trading, adds analyst comment)

* Indexes down: Dow 1.08%, S&P 500 2.08%, Nasdaq 3.37%

* Intel ( INTC ) slides after reporting big cash burn

* Crypto firms slide after reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance

By Stephen Culp and Purvi Agarwal

NEW YORK, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US stocks tumbled on Friday, with the Nasdaq plunging to a three-month low following disappointing quarterly results from Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), which amplified growing fears surrounding AI-related companies' massive spending on the nascent technology, and concerns about when or whether the cash burn will start to pay off.

All three major US stock indexes slumped, with the Nasdaq sliding 3.4%. The tech-heavy index has dropped more than 8% from its all-time closing high reached on October 6.

The tech rout was sparked by disappointing quarterly results from Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) released late on Thursday. The companies' shares slumped 2.1% and 30.9%, respectively.

Chip stocks veered sharply lower, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) down 5.3% and AMD sliding 12.1%. The broader chips index shed 8.7% and was headed for a monthly loss. Server makers Dell and HP lost 12.5% and 10.8%, respectively.

Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) were set to wipe out nearly $200 billion in combined market value if losses hold, setting up the Nasdaq-100 to erase over $1 trillion on Friday.

"It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York.

"Companies that are performing and meeting the very lofty expectations that have been set are doing well," Pursche added. "Those that are falling short and seem to be missing the mark or not executing as expected are getting punished."

The selloff put all three indexes on course to close lower on the week. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq are on track to log monthly losses, while the Dow appears set to end October with a gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 566.81 points, or 1.08%, to 51,778.86, the S&P 500 lost 160.54 points, or 2.08%, to 7,559.85 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 881.35 points, or 3.37%, to 25,303.37.

The S&P 500 tech sector was on track for its largest monthly percentage loss since March 2025, and communication services looked to be headed for its biggest monthly drop since April 2022.

Third-quarter earnings season has passed the halfway mark, with 299 companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 82% have beaten consensus expectations, according to LSEG data.

Analysts now expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.6%, year-on-year, per LSEG.

Oil supermajors Exxon Mobil and Chevron ( CVX ) both beat quarterly profit expectations, benefiting from soaring profit margins as a result of energy supply disruptions arising from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine. The stocks gained 1.7% and 1.4%, respectively.

Starbucks ( SBUX ) slid 1.4% after the coffee chain forecast an annual revenue decline due to its divestiture of its Chinese business.

Cryptocurrency-related firms Coinbase, Strategy , and Robinhood fell between 8.8% and 13.6% in the wake of reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.8-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. There were 147 new highs and 298 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,144 stocks rose and 3,559 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.11-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 43 new 52-week highs and five new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 62 new highs and 290 new lows.

(Reporting by Stephen Culp in New York; Additional reporting by Shashwat Chauhan, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: US judge orders ethics investigation into DOJ lawyers in golf course dispute
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US District Judge Ana Reyes on Friday ordered an investigation into whether Department of Justice attorneys violated ethics rules in their defense of a lawsuit filed over President Donald Trump's planned renovation of a Washington-area golf course.

Reyes expressed concerns during a hearing in Washington federal court that the attorneys had misrepresented the government's intention to continue with the renovation of the East Potomac Golf Links after she temporarily blocked the project.

Reyes grilled DOJ attorney Stanley Woodward for more than two hours over potentially contradictory statements by Trump and the department's lawyers about the government's intentions. She said she was concerned the attorneys had provided "materially misleading information" and omitted other relevant information about the administration's plans, and appointed a special master to investigate further.

Reyes also ordered the attorneys to preserve relevant documents.

"For months, the court trusted but did not verify," Reyes said. "No longer."

Trump's renovation of the golf course is one of several projects ​the president is pursuing to reshape landmarks in the US capital. The DC Preservation League sued in February to halt the administration's takeover of the course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American ​history."

Reyes said in May that the government must provide advance notice ​of any substantive construction work at the course. After the administration removed hundreds of trees without notice in October, she issued a temporary order blocking further tree removal and said defiance would result in proceedings to determine whether government officials should be held in contempt.

Trump later said his administration would begin renovation work immediately, despite the judge's order. Reyes extended her order days later, after which Trump said in an online post that his administration would close the course site "as scheduled on November ​15th in order to renovate and rebuild."

Reyes has said the ​government had ⁠asked her to disregard Trump's statements about the renovation plans. The Department of Justice has told the court that no final plan exists to replace the course.

"The third-highest ranking official in the Department of Justice is telling a federal court that he cannot say, when the president has said 'the course will close on November 15,' what he meant was, 'the course will close on November 15?'" Reyes asked Woodward during the hearing.

(Reporting by Blake Brittain in Washington, Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi and David Gregorio)

Big Tech stocks sold off this week as companies disclosed they are burning through cash to fuel their AI expansion at a time when interest rates are rising, raising questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

David Woodcock, who became SEC enforcement director in May, said the agency does not want to stand in the way of tech innovation, but that it is the agency's job to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks. 

"Our principal concern is that people are making accurate disclosures about material information so that investors know what they're getting into," Woodcock said in an interview. "Enforcement is a very necessary piece of making sure people are doing that."

Where such disclosure does not happen, "then enforcement will be present," he said.

Woodcock also said that AI and superintelligence have made scams much easier and cheaper to manufacture at scale, raising risks for more and more people. Brokers and other firms need to have processes in place to protect retail investors and "take thoughtful action," he said.

data.title: Fed needs at least two more rate hikes, Logan says
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The Federal Reserve needs to raise rates at least two more times to get inflation under control, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said on Friday, in some of the most explicit rate guidance offered by a US central banker since Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh took the helm in May.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said in remarks prepared for delivery to students at Davidson College, referring to the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee. "After that, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate."

Logan joined the majority of the FOMC in a 10-2 vote this week to leave short-term US interest rates in their current 3.75%-4.00% range, even as it said the economy is strong and inflation too high.

For Logan, among the more hawkish of Fed policymakers, the move isn't inconsistent with her view that the target rate should be at least half a percentage point higher in order to restrict the economy enough to get inflation headed back to the Fed's 2% goal. 

"Financial markets have been volatile in response to news on the technology investment outlook and geopolitical developments," Logan said. "In such an environment, adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary."

It's important that the Fed make its policy destination clear though, Logan said -- a view that contrasts with Warsh's insistence that the Fed should only deliver such guidance in crisis times. 

For one thing, Logan sees financial conditions as delivering a tailwind to economic growth, and attributes the recent rise in longer-term borrowing costs to an expectation for stronger growth and higher interest rates.

"The higher market rates are more a message that investors believe monetary policy has work to do than an independent headwind for activity," she said. Skipping a meeting, she said, does not change the Fed's policy destination. 

"As long as market participants understand the FOMC's policy plans, the precise timing of each rate increase has little effect on the longer-term rates most borrowers pay," she said.

(Reporting by Ann Saphir; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: Nasdaq hits near three-month low as Amazon, Intel rattle AI trade
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq fell to its lowest in nearly three months on Friday after Amazon's ( AMZN ) aggressive AI spending plans and Intel's ( INTC ) cash-burn warning heightened concerns over soaring AI buildout costs and the timeline for returns.

After paring most of its premarket declines, Amazon.com ( AMZN ) was down 2%. The company reported a sharp cash outflow in the third quarter and signaled another increase in capital expenditure next year.

Intel ( INTC ) was set for its steepest one-day drop on record with a near 29% slide after the chipmaker said it would burn cash this year due to a weak PC market, manufacturing hurdles and heavy spending to expand production.

The warning sparked a selloff in global chip stocks, with Nvidia down 3.7% and AMD sliding about 10%. The broader chips index shed 7%. Server makers Dell and HP lost 10.4% and 8.7%, respectively.

Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) were set to wipe out near $200 billion in combined market value, if losses hold, setting up the Nasdaq-100 to erase just over $1 trillion on Friday. The index is set to shed more than $2 trillion this month.

"A lot of them kind of got ahead of themselves. It's all earnings based and right now, they're not producing," said Joe Saluzzi, co-manager of trading at Themis Trading.

"Though it's having a terrible day, Intel ( INTC ) is still up significantly this year. It (the decline) doesn't kill the whole story, it's pretty much a reset."

The S&P 500 information technology index was the biggest drag, down 3.9% and set for its steepest one-day fall since June 23. The communication services index was headed for its worst month since April 2022.

data.title: Imperial Oil considering moving ahead with Aspen oil sands project earlier than planned
data.description:
* Aspen could produce up to 150,000 barrels of bitumen per day

* Decision timing depends on technology readiness, fiscal and regulatory environment

* Imperial still targeting mid-November for Pathways carbon capture agreements

By Amanda Stephenson and Khusbu Jena

Oct 30 (Reuters) - Canada's Imperial Oil ( IMO ) is considering a decision to proceed with its Aspen oil sands project earlier than planned.

Exxon-owned Imperial had previously said it would make a final investment decision on the Aspen project at the end of this decade. But CEO John Whelan said on a conference call Friday the company is considering making a decision sooner on Aspen, a major proposed new oil sands development in northern Alberta that could produce up to 150,000 barrels of bitumen per day. It would be among Imperial's largest sources of oil.

"We are looking at do we want to bring it forward," Whelan said.

The announcement is a sign of growing confidence among Canadian oil sands producers in the wake of Prime Minister Mark Carney's efforts to boost Canadian oil production and grow the country's economy. Carney has repealed many of the environmental policies of his predecessor Justin Trudeau. He also has cut the tax rate on new capital investment, and pledged to back a new proposed crude pipeline to the country's west coast.

Canada is the world's fourth-largest oil producer, and its oil production has been rising. But the last major new oil sands project, Suncor's Fort Hills, started operating in 2018. Since then, companies have concentrated on smaller expansions of existing projects and have been reluctant to make the kind of major new capital investments that spur job creation and economic growth.

While no oil sands producer has yet committed to a major expansion, Whelan said Imperial is encouraged by steps taken by both the federal and Alberta provincial governments so far this year to improve the investment environment for Canadian oil.

He said ​oil sands companies continue to target mid-November as their preferred time frame to reach definitive agreements with the Alberta and federal governments, paving the way for a potential decision to construct the multi-billion-dollar Pathways carbon capture project. Carney has said this must be a prerequisite to the west coast pipeline going ahead.

Imperial's proposed Aspen development is an in situ project, meaning it would use steam to loosen the thick bitumen located in Alberta's oil sands in order to bring it to the surface. The company is working on a pilot project on the Aspen site that will make use of solvent-assisted technology to significantly reduce the amount of steam required - reducing both greenhouse gas emissions and water usage.

Whelan said Imperial's long-term plan is to use the solvent-assisted technology at two of its other undeveloped in situ lease sites, Corner and Clarke Creek. Taken together with Aspen, Whelan said, the three projects have the potential to double the company's upstream production over time.

"Ultimately our decision (to move the Aspen timing forward) is going to be driven by technology readiness, project economics and again, that broader fiscal and regulatory environment," he said.

Imperial posted an adjusted net income of C$5.11 per share for the quarter ended September 30, beating analysts' average estimate of C$4.70 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Total throughput volumes, or the amount of crude processed, fell to 381,000 barrels per day during the third quarter from 425,000 bpd a year ago, hurt by an 18-day production halt at its Kearl oil sands facility that was caused by a transformer failure at the Enbridge ( ENB )-operated Woodland Pipeline.

Quarterly upstream production averaged 418,000 gross barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), lower than 462,000 gross boepd a year earlier, due to the third-party pipeline outage and planned turnarounds at its three Alberta assets.

($1 = 1.3959 Canadian dollars)

(Reporting by Amanda Stephenson in Calgary and Khusbu Jena in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid and David Gregorio)

data.title: Exxon, Chevron profits beat forecasts, refining margins surge during wars
data.description:
* Exxon earns more from refining than from upstream in Q3

* Chevron's ( CVX ) Q3 downstream earnings reach highest point in at least six years

* Both companies use excess cash to pay down debt

* BP beats profit estimates, will pay remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities

By Sheila Dang

HOUSTON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - ExxonMobil ( XOM ) and Chevron ( CVX ) both beat analyst expectations for quarterly profit on Friday, as soaring refining margins increased earnings from their fuel-making businesses - which typically have smaller profits - to rival the upstream segments.

The results capped off a second straight banner quarter for Big Oil, with sharply higher gasoline and diesel prices during the US-Israeli war with Iran and the war between Russia and Ukraine which have disrupted global energy markets.

Shares of both companies rose nearly 2% on Friday in line with the broader S&P 500 energy index, even as Wall Street's major indexes fell.

The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz and recent attacks on refineries in Saudi Arabia and Russia have knocked out fuel-making capacity, sending refining margins sky-high, and Western oil majors' earnings have boomed.

Shell, TotalEnergies and BP also topped third-quarter profit estimates this week. BP reached a record.

For the first time in at least six years, Exxon, the largest US oil producer by market capitalization, has been earning more from refining than from exploration and drilling. Chevron's ( CVX ) third-quarter downstream earnings also reached their highest point over the same time frame.

Fuel-making margins should return to more normal levels when conflicts end and damaged refineries are repaired, but that will take time, executives from both companies said.

"Margins will stay a bit elevated, maybe into next year," Chevron ( CVX ) Vice Chairman Mark Nelson said during a conference call with analysts.

INCREASING FUEL SUPPLIES

Exxon is investing more in its refineries, including at its Baytown complex in Texas, to increase fuel production, and has leaned on its trading team to direct supplies to where they are needed globally, Chief Financial Officer Neil Hansen said in an interview.

"It's important to acknowledge that these higher fuel prices put real pressure on families and businesses," he said. "The most meaningful response ... that we can offer as a company is to pull every lever that's available to us to increase supply."

Distillate production in the US will grow by another 100,000 barrels per day through the refinery investments, the company said, without giving a timeline.

Exxon CEO Darren Woods said the company is looking for more ways to expand its existing refining facilities, along with upgrading them to produce more fuels or chemical feedstocks.

The high cost of diesel and gasoline is among voters' biggest frustrations ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections.

Chevron ( CVX ) has opportunities to increase efficiency at its US Gulf refineries and could grow capacity by 7% at its Pascagoula refinery in Mississippi by the end of the decade, Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner told Reuters in an interview.

Exxon reported third-quarter adjusted earnings per share of $4.23, while Chevron ( CVX ) earned $5.28 in adjusted per-share profit.

PAYING DOWN DEBT

The two US oil majors are using the cash windfall to pay down debt and strengthen their balance sheets instead of significantly raising dividends or buying back more shares.

UK oil producer BP said it would put higher earnings toward slashing liabilities, including an early repayment of its outstanding $5 billion post-tax bill for the 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster that killed 11 people.

Exxon reduced debt by $8 billion during the third quarter, Hansen said, adding it planned to stick to its approach of maintaining and growing its dividend over the long term. The company raised its fourth-quarter dividend by 4 cents from the previous quarter.

Chevron ( CVX ) has cut net debt by nearly $14 billion from the end of 2025.

"We think in decades, not quarters," Bonner said. "We need that (strong) balance sheet through high prices and low prices."

Bonner said the spot price of benchmark Brent crude swung from as low as $68 per barrel to a high of $132 during the market's volatile third quarter.

Exxon said it would repurchase $20 billion worth of shares in 2027, the same level as in the previous two years.

(Reporting by Sheila Dang in Houston; Additional reporting by Shadia Nasralla, Pooja Menon and Arunima Kumar; Editing by Tomasz Janowski, David Holmes, David Gaffen and David Gregorio)

In economic news, France's consumer price index in October is expected to rise 3.4% on year, while Q3 real gross domestic product contracted by 0.1% on quarter and on year, said the country's statistical office Insee.

Separately, the seasonally adjusted Q3 Eurozone gross domestic product rose 0.4% on quarter, while the broader EU's economy expanded by 0.5%, Eurostat reported. On the year, GDP rose by 1.3% in the Eurozone and by 1.5% in the EU.

In regulatory news, Meta, TikTok and X lost a legal challenge against UK regulator Ofcom over information requests under the UK's Online Safety Act, according to the court document on Friday. The UK High Court upheld Ofcom's requests for content moderation data, it added. The Online Safety Act 2023 requires internet services to manage risks from illegal and harmful content, particularly material affecting children, the document said.

In corporate news, BP CEO Meg O'Neill categorically denied conversations about breaking up the company, reaffirming the importance of its integrated oil and gas business during the Q3 earnings call Friday. O'Neill said discussions with the board about BP's strategic direction reinforced the importance of an integrated model, with upstream, downstream and trading operations generating value together. She said the combined business generates more value than its individual components, with strong results across all three segments in the quarter demonstrating the benefits of integration. BP reported Q3 underlying replacement cost profit Friday of $3.26 per diluted American depositary share, up from $0.85 a year earlier. BP shares rose 0.5% in London.

TotalEnergies said Friday it will cut diesel prices to 2.15 euros ($2.41) per liter, at 705 of its access service-stations in France, starting Saturday. The access stations represent about 60% of company fuel sales, TotalEnergies said. Separately, TotalEnergies has signed a farm-out deal to sell a 40% participating stake in the OPL257 block offshore Nigeria to South Atlantic Petroleum, TotalEnergies said Friday. Following the deal's completion, TotalEnergies will own a 50% operated interest in the block, while Conoil will hold the remaining 10%. TotalEnergies shares were up 1% in Paris.

The field has a capacity of 250 million standard cubic feet per day, with gas processed at the Jangkrik Floating Production Unit and supplied to domestic markets and the Bontang plant for LNG production, the company said. data.title: AutoNation's Quarterly Revenue Tops Views on After-Sales Growth
data.description:
01:12 PM EDT, 10/30/2026 (MT Newswires) -- AutoNation's ( AN ) third-quarter revenue topped Wall Street's projections as gains in its after-sales business helped offset soft new vehicle sales, sending its shares higher on Friday.

The automotive retailer's September-quarter revenue slipped to $7.01 billion from $7.04 billion a year earlier, but surpassed the FactSet-polled consensus of $6.93 billion. Adjusted per-share earnings rose to $5.11 from $5.01, while analysts expected $5.08.

The stock was up 5.3% intraday, trimming its year-to-date losses to 14%.

Revenue from the parts and service business, which represents the after-sales segment, rose 5.2% to $1.29 billion.

New vehicle revenue fell 2.5% year over year to $3.33 billion, while used vehicle sales rose 1% to $2.04 billion.

"Vehicle volumes were lower year over year, primarily reflecting the comparison with demand ahead of the September 2025 (electric vehicle) incentive expiration and last year's tariff announcements," Chief Financial Officer Thomas Szlosek said during an earnings conference call, according to a FactSet transcript said. "This is behind us as we move forward, but it did create a $0.52 per share unfavorable impact in the quarter."

After-sales and AutoNation Finance contributed $0.38 and $0.27 to EPS growth, respectively, Szlosek told analysts.

The results also benefited from the company's share repurchase activities, Chief Executive Mike Manley said on the call.

Last month, AutoNation ( AN ) rival CarMax ( KMX ) reported stronger-than-expected fiscal second-quarter revenue buoyed by a double-digit increase in comparable used-vehicle sales amid early momentum in the company's growth plan. Late Wednesday, Carvana ( CVNA ) said it is poised for a "strong finish" to 2026 following its third-quarter performance.

UBS Securities recently said that a modest increase in interest rates is unlikely to dampen auto demand, though it could still hurt dealers in particular due to their floating debt structure.

Last month, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points to cool inflation, which marked the US central bank's first rate hike in just over three years. It kept interest rates steady this week, but is widely anticipated to hike again in December.

The auto financing businesses of AutoNation ( AN ), CarMax ( KMX ) and Lithia Motors ( LAD ) have floating and refinancing debt components, UBS said in a note earlier this month.
